svg.title: Azure Document OCR — Platform Architecture
svg.desc: Approved platform documents become searchable text through controlled indexing.

g.text: Approved platform documents become searchable text through controlled indexing.
Staff sign-in and API access tokens.
Current account, staff and role checks.
Retain the exact uploaded source bytes.
Upload alone does not approve OCR.
Revisions, job queue and lease metadata.
Index timer in the API host
Five-minute UTC timer or Admin action.
Claims one eligible SQL indexing job.
Storage queue + scanner save exact proof.
Refresh rights; verify lease and source.
Match Blob version, ETag, size and hash.
Read existing PDF, DOCX and text content.
Without OCR, only readable text remains.
Unknown work keeps its charge hold.
API managed identity; one analysis POST.
Whole file sent; selected pages processed.
Save the Azure operation receipt in SQL.
Poll that exact operation using GET.
Check selected pages and text bounds.
Keep blank pages and true page numbers.
Merge local/OCR text; chunk and publish.
Recheck lease, source and policy revision.
Private endpoint/DNS reach the AI account.
No OpenAI badge key is used for OCR.
Recognized text is stored in Azure SQL for retrieval; the original Blob/PDF is retained unchanged. This does not add a searchable layer to the PDF.
A clean upload, approved search policy, completed OCR and published index are separate states. Blank-only content cannot become useful indexed evidence.
The saved receipt does not provide automatic post-restart resumption. Uncertain submission or lease state requires review, never a blind second POST.
Storage scan queues belong to the existing Defender pipeline; RAG indexing jobs and leases are in SQL. No dedicated OCR worker is deployed.
Architecture, not a live health check: native extraction can bypass OCR; independent server/source flags and private service readiness still apply.
